note: RESEARCHED sizes from public Hyderabad market data, collected 2026-09-20. NOT the firm's own blocks. Method: 10 real 2BHK/3BHK examples were collected from mainstream Hyderabad group-housing projects (My Home Avatar, Rajapushpa Provincia, ASBL Spire, Prestige City Hyderabad, Aparna Sarovar Zenith, Candeur Lakescape, Vasavi Urban, Vertex Panache, Vertex Viraat, NCC Urban One), then reduced to the 4 representative types below. Each type's saleable_sqft is a real advertised figure from a named project, not an average. NO floor plan, brochure, image or CAD file was copied; only published numbers were recorded. Sources per type: 2BHK-A = Aparna Sarovar Zenith 1275 sqft (squareyards.com/hyderabad-residential-property/aparna-sarovar-zenith/100065/project), corroborated by Vertex Panache 1270 sqft. 2BHK-B = Rajapushpa Provincia 1370 sqft, developer's own site (rajapushpa.in/projects/residential/rajapushpaprovincia.php). 3BHK-A = Rajapushpa Provincia 1715 sqft, same developer source. 3BHK-B = ASBL Spire 1905 sqft, developer's own plan page (asbl.in/spire/plan/plans/), the single best data point found because ASBL publishes the full breakdown: RERA carpet 1186 + balcony 147 + external wall 138 + common area 434 = 1905 saleable. CONFIDENCE: 2BHK-B, 3BHK-A and 3BHK-B come from developers' own websites (high); 2BHK-A comes from a listing portal (medium). GEOMETRY IS ASSUMED, AREAS ARE REAL. No public source published a flat's overall footprint dimensions, so width and depth could not be read from the market; they are derived. depth_m = 11.0 m for every flat is taken from the firm's own Dhulapally area statement, whose tower depth of 24.13 m = 2 x 11.0 + 2.13 m corridor. width_m is then solved so that width x depth x 10.7639 x 1.22 reproduces the advertised saleable area (all four round-trip to within 0.5 sqft). LOADING FACTOR = 22% from flat footprint to saleable, i.e. saleable = (footprint area) x 1.22. This is the loading the firm's own area statement uses and sits inside the 20-25% band. Note the trap: ASBL's published breakdown gives 1905/1186 = 61% if measured CARPET to saleable, but carpet excludes balcony and external walls; measured FOOTPRINT to saleable it is 1905/1471 = 29.5%. The engine needs the footprint ratio, not the carpet ratio. If the firm's true loading is 30% rather than 22%, every width below shrinks by about 6%. TREAT THE WIDTHS AS CALIBRATED ASSUMPTIONS, NOT AS MEASURED BLOCKS; replace with the firm's DWG blocks when they arrive.
